prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild the public-domain woodblock print as a self-contained, animated low-poly 3D wallpaper; record boat count and mountain in JSON.

[action] Inspected `./print.jpg` (Hokusai, *The Great Wave off Kanagawa*). Built `./scene/index.html` from code only: procedural low-poly Great Wave with foam crest/claw, three oshiokuri-bune boats with rowers, snow-capped Mount Fuji, paper sky, indigo/cream palette, cartouche, generated paper grain, and gentle wave, spray, boat and cloud motion. Wrote `./result.json`; loaded the file in a browser and verified `__sceneReady === true`, then closed the tab/session. Only Google Fonts and the pinned three.js CDN are referenced.

[result] Delivered `scene/index.html` (no build step) and `result.json`:
- Boats: **3** (left face of the wave, trough left of the mountain, right foreground).
- Mountain: **Mount Fuji**.
- Knowledge basis: direct visual inspection of the JPEG — three hulls are visible and the cartouche reads 冨嶽三十六景 神奈川沖浪裏 ("Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji: Under the Wave off Kanagawa"), which names the mountain; the tiny snow-capped peak in the trough matches it.

[next] Open `scene/index.html` directly in the browser; nothing to install. Assumption: "copies it" means recognizable composition/palette/subjects rebuilt as original low-poly geometry, not a traced texture.
